# Get started on ThreadX in QEMU (RISC-V 64)

<!-- type: how-to · level: 1 -->

**Needs first:** [Install](../start/install.md)

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED by scripts/gen-board-support.py: starter status -->
> **Status:** Verified in emulator (daily). From the board support registry: [`nros-board-threadx-qemu-riscv64`](../reference/boards/threadx-qemu-riscv64.md); [Board Support Levels](../reference/board-support-levels.md) explains the words.
<!-- END GENERATED starter status -->

This starter puts a Rust talker on Eclipse ThreadX (formerly Azure RTOS
ThreadX), on QEMU's 64-bit RISC-V `virt` machine, and shows its messages
arriving in ROS 2. ThreadX runs the talker as a thread, with NetX Duo as its
TCP/IP stack on a virtio-net device. You install no RISC-V cross-compiler and
no QEMU of your own: `nros setup` fetches both.

## What you need

- A Linux host with the [install](../start/install.md) done, so `nros` is on
  your `PATH`.
- ROS 2 Humble with `ros-humble-rmw-zenoh-cpp`. ROS 2 provides the zenoh
  router the board talks to, and the message definitions the build generates
  the talker's code from.

No board, no cable and no root access: QEMU's user-mode network carries the
guest's ethernet to your machine, with no TAP device to create. WiFi is
deferred to the Zephyr 4.4 line, so no starter opens over WiFi yet.

## Provision

```bash probe=30
nros setup rv-virt-threadx --rmw zenoh
```

That fetches the RISC-V 64 cross-compiler, the `qemu-system-riscv64` that
emulates the machine, and the ThreadX and NetX Duo sources into a shared store
under `~/.nros`. Most of it is prebuilt for your host; what is not is built
from source the first time, and `nros setup --dry-run` shows which. It
installs no router: the router is ROS's `rmw_zenohd`.

## Scaffold the project

```bash probe=40
nros new tx_ws --board rv-virt-threadx --template talker --lang rust
cd tx_ws
```

That wrote a workspace with two packages:

```text
tx_ws/
└── src/
    ├── tx_node/                 # the talker: package.xml, Cargo.toml (a library), src/lib.rs
    └── tx_node_bringup/         # package.xml and system.toml: the board, the RMW, the node
```

`tx_node` is the talker, a library with no `main()` that names no board. It
publishes `std_msgs/String` on `/chatter` once a second. `tx_node_bringup`
says what the talker runs on. The ThreadX startup that runs your node is
generated from it when you build, so you do not need to open it for this
starter.

## Run it in QEMU

The guest sits on QEMU's user-mode network and dials the router through the
gateway `10.0.2.2`, which is your host, on port 7447. Start the router first,
in its own terminal, listening on every interface so the guest's connection
arrives:

<!-- removed when the board descriptor states its default locator -->
```bash probe=50 probe-run=60 probe-keep
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
ZENOH_CONFIG_OVERRIDE='listen/endpoints=["tcp/0.0.0.0:7447"];scouting/multicast/enabled=false' \
    ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd
```

```text probe-expect=50
Started Zenoh router with id
```

Then, in a second terminal, in the workspace, source ROS 2 and build and run
the talker. This first run records the ROS 2 prefix in the workspace, so
later runs of it need no sourced shell:

```bash probe=60 probe-run=1500
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
nros run tx_node --expect 'Publishing:'
```

```text probe-expect=60
Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'
nros run: matched after
```

`nros run` builds the firmware (the first build compiles ThreadX, NetX Duo
and nano-ros, a few minutes; later builds take seconds), then boots it with
the store's `qemu-system-riscv64` on the `virt` machine, the UART on your
terminal and virtio-net on the user-mode network. What it prints is the
board's console. With `--expect` it stops QEMU and exits 0 at the first
console line containing that text, and exits 1 if the board stops first. The
router keeps running.

Without `--expect` it keeps running until you press Ctrl-C, which stops QEMU:

```bash probe=65 probe-run=150 probe-keep
nros run tx_node
```

```text probe-expect=65
Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'
Publishing: 'Hello World: 2'
```

## See it in ROS 2

Leave the router and `nros run` going. In a third terminal:

```bash probe=70 probe-run=90
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 topic echo /chatter std_msgs/msg/String --qos-reliability best_effort
```

```text probe-expect=70
data: 'Hello World:
```

The talker publishes best-effort, and `ros2 topic echo` defaults to reliable,
which receives nothing from it. That is why the command asks for best-effort.

## If it doesn't work

- **No `Publishing:` line within 30 seconds of boot:** the talker did not
  reach the router. QEMU's boot and NetX Duo's start take about 15 seconds.
  Check that the router listens on `0.0.0.0:7447`: one on `127.0.0.1` is out
  of the guest's reach.
- **`nros run` stops at once and names `AMENT_PREFIX_PATH`:** this shell has
  not sourced ROS 2, and no earlier build of the workspace recorded it.
- **`nros run` names no `qemu-system-riscv64`:** run the `nros setup
  rv-virt-threadx` step again, which installs it.
- **Everything else:** [Troubleshooting - First 10 Minutes](../reference/troubleshooting-index.md).
